parent_districts_1998_names: ABBOTTABAD DISTRICT; HARIPUR DISTRICT; MANSEHRA DISTRICT; BATAGRAM DISTRICT; KOHISTAN DISTRICT (part)
former_names: Hazara District (Abbottabad and Haripur tehsils)
notes: Created in 1976 when Hazara District was bifurcated into Abbottabad (Abbottabad and Haripur tehsils) and Mansehra districts; the PCO document cited in Wikipedia gives 30 June 1976 while the Wikipedia infobox gives 1 October 1976 (uncited), and Haripur tehsil was separated from it in 1991.
source_title: Abbottabad District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Abbottabad (PCO 1999); Haripur District (Wikipedia) citing PCO '1951-98 Population of Administrative Units' for the 30 June 1976 date

notes: British-era settled district (one of the five NWFP settled districts of 1901) that existed at every census; Lakki Marwat (Marwat tehsil) was carved out of it on 1 July 1992, so its pre-1998 populations were restated by PCO.
source_title: List of districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Wikipedia), history section citing the 1901 NWFP settled districts and the PCO census tables

former_names: Batagram tehsil/sub-division of Mansehra District (of Hazara District before 1976; tribal Yaghistan area merged as a tehsil in 1955)
notes: Separated from Mansehra District in July 1993 and given district status; it was a tehsil of Hazara from 1955 and of Mansehra from 1976, which is consistent with PCO having no 1951 population for it.
source_title: Battagram District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Batagram (PCO 1999) p. 18; Mansehra District and Hazara Division (Wikipedia) also give 1993

former_names: Buner tehsil of Swat District (part of Swat State until 1969)
notes: Buner was a tehsil of Swat District until it was given district status in 1991.
source_title: Buner District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Buner (PCO 2000); Dawn 'Before merger' 19 Apr 2018 (https://www.dawn.com/news/1402508) also gives 1991

former_names: Charsadda tehsil of Peshawar District
notes: Charsadda tehsil of Peshawar District was upgraded to a district in 1988 (1 July 1988 per a local history blog); English Wikipedia prints 1998 while French Wikipedia prints 1988 citing the same 1998 District Census Report p. 1, and PCO lists it as a district at the 1 March 1998 census, so 1988 is taken as the year but should be checked against the DCR.
source_title: District de Charsadda (fr.wikipedia), citing PCO 1998 District Census Report of Charsadda p. 1; charsaddahistory.blogspot.com gives 1 July 1988; en.wikipedia Charsadda District prints 1998

former_names: Chitral State (princely state under Malakand Agency)
notes: Chitral State was merged under the Dir, Chitral and Swat Administration Regulation of 1969 and became a district; some sources date district status to 1970 when Malakand Division was formed, and PCO restated the 1951 and 1961 state populations onto the district.
source_title: Kingdom of Chitral (Wikipedia), citing Long et al. 2015 and Osella 2010; Malakand Division (Wikipedia) gives 1970 for district formation

former_names: Dera Ismail Khan District
notes: British-era settled district (one of the five NWFP settled districts of 1901) that existed at every census; Tank tehsil was carved out of it in 1992.
source_title: List of districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Wikipedia), history section citing the 1901 NWFP settled districts and the PCO census tables

former_names: Hangu tehsil of Kohat District
notes: Hangu tehsil was carved out of Kohat District on 30 June 1996 according to Wikipedia (uncited), and it existed as a district at the 1 March 1998 census because PCO lists it among the 24 NWFP districts with restated populations; the 1998 date sometimes quoted is therefore too late.
source_title: Hangu District, Pakistan (Wikipedia), 30 June 1996 uncited; Kohat Division (Wikipedia) citing PCO '1951-98 Population of Administrative Units' places the upgrade between the 1981 and 1998 censuses

former_names: Haripur tehsil of Abbottabad District (of Hazara District before 1976)
notes: Haripur tehsil was split off from Abbottabad District in July 1991 to form Haripur District.
source_title: Haripur District (Wikipedia), citing Abbasi et al. 2022 PJSR; Abbottabad District (Wikipedia) citing 1998 District Census Report of Abbottabad; Hazara Division (Wikipedia) gives July 1991

former_names: Karak tehsil (formerly Teri tehsil) of Kohat District
notes: Karak gained district status in 1982, before which it was the Karak (formerly Teri) tehsil of Kohat District.
source_title: Karak District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Karak (PCO 2000); Kohat Division (Wikipedia) for the Teri name

notes: British-era settled district (one of the five NWFP settled districts of 1901) that existed at every census; Karak (1982) and Hangu (1996) were carved out of it, and Orakzai Agency (1973) out of its Frontier Region.
source_title: List of districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Wikipedia), history section citing the 1901 NWFP settled districts and the PCO census tables

former_names: Swat Kohistan (Swat District, formerly Swat State) and Hazara/Indus Kohistan (Hazara District, Mansehra side)
notes: Kohistan was notified as a district in 1976 (1 October 1976 per the Wikipedia infobox, uncited) from the Kohistan tracts of Swat District and of Hazara District; the parent attribution rests on the Wikipedia district list only, and PCO has no 1951 or 1961 population for it.
source_title: Dawn, 'KP govt creates new Kohistan district', 16 Jan 2014 ('Notified as a district in 1976'); Kohistan District (Wikipedia) infobox 1 October 1976; List of districts in KP (Wikipedia) for parents

former_names: Lakki Marwat tehsil (formerly Marwat tehsil) of Bannu District
notes: Lakki Marwat was created as a district on 1 July 1992, before which it was the Marwat/Lakki Marwat tehsil of Bannu District.
source_title: Lakki Marwat District (Wikipedia), 1 July 1992 with 1998 District Census Report of Lakki Marwat (PCO 2000) in references; Bannu Division (Wikipedia) citing PCO 1951-98 places the upgrade between the 1981 and 1998 censuses

former_names: Dir District (southern part; Dir State until 1969)
notes: Formed in 1996 when Dir District was divided into Upper Dir and Lower Dir; Dir State was merged in 1969 and became a district in 1970; parent is given as UPPER DIR DISTRICT because that is the 1998 name carried by the remainder of the old Dir District.
source_title: Lower Dir District (Wikipedia), citing Deputy Commissioner Dir Lower 'About District' (dirlower.kp.gov.pk); Upper Dir District and Dir (region) (Wikipedia) also give 1996

former_names: Malakand Protected Area (tract of Malakand Agency); Malakand Agency
notes: The Malakand Protected Area around Malakand Fort was a tract of Malakand Agency until the agency became Malakand Division in 1970, when the tract became a Provincially Administered Tribal Area (Malakand Agency/Protected Area) at district level; one Wikipedia page dates this to 1969, and PCO restated 1951 and 1961 populations for the tract although it was not a district-level unit then.
source_title: Malakand Agency (Wikipedia); Malakand Division (Wikipedia) citing Jamestown Foundation 'Profile of Pakistan's Tribal Areas'; Malakand District (Wikipedia) gives 1969

parent_districts_1998_names: ABBOTTABAD DISTRICT; HARIPUR DISTRICT; MANSEHRA DISTRICT; BATAGRAM DISTRICT; KOHISTAN DISTRICT (part)
former_names: Hazara District (Mansehra tehsil, including Batagram sub-division; Amb State merged 1969)
notes: Mansehra was established as a district in 1976 (October 1976 per Hazara Division page) when Hazara District was bifurcated; Batagram was separated from it in July 1993 and the Hazara Kohistan tract went to Kohistan District in 1976.
source_title: Mansehra District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Mansehra (PCO 2000) p. 1; Hazara District (Wikipedia) citing the same DCR; Hazara Division (Wikipedia) for October 1976

former_names: Mardan and Swabi tehsils of Peshawar District
notes: Mardan was created in 1937 by bifurcating Peshawar District, so it existed at every post-1947 census; Swabi tehsil was carved out of it in 1988.
source_title: Mardan District (Wikipedia); SMEDA 'Districts Profile Mardan' (https://smeda.org/phocadownload/Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa/Districts_Profile_Mardan.pdf) also gives 1937

former_names: Nowshera tehsil of Peshawar District
notes: Nowshera tehsil of Peshawar District was upgraded to a district in 1988 (Wikipedia says between 1988 and 1990 citing the 1998 DCR; travelmypakistan says 1988).
source_title: Nowshera District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Nowshera (PCO 1999); travelmypakistan.com Nowshera page (https://www.travelmypakistan.com/?p=184) gives 1988

notes: British-era settled district (one of the five NWFP settled districts of 1901) that existed at every census; Mardan (1937), Charsadda (1988) and Nowshera (1988) were carved out of it.
source_title: List of districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Wikipedia), history section citing the 1901 NWFP settled districts and the PCO census tables

former_names: Shangla (Alpuri) sub-division of Swat District (part of Swat State until 1969)
notes: Shangla was a sub-division of Swat District until it was given separate district status in 1995.
source_title: Shangla District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Shangla (PCO 2000); Dawn 'Before merger' 19 Apr 2018 (https://www.dawn.com/news/1402508) also gives 1995

former_names: Swabi tehsil of Mardan District (of Peshawar District before 1937)
notes: Swabi was a tehsil of Mardan District until it became a district in 1988.
source_title: Swabi District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Swabi (PCO 2000) p. 1; SMEDA 'Districts Profile Mardan' says carved out of Mardan in the 1980s

former_names: Swat State (princely state under Malakand Agency)
notes: Swat State was merged into West Pakistan/NWFP in 1969 under the Dir, Chitral and Swat Administration Regulation and became Swat District (1970 per the Malakand Division page); Buner (1991), Shangla (1995) and the Swat Kohistan tract (to Kohistan, 1976) were later carved out, and PCO restated the 1951 and 1961 state populations onto the 1998 districts.
source_title: Swat District (Wikipedia), citing Sultan-i-Rome 2008 'Swat State, 1915-1969, From Genesis to Merger'; Malakand Division (Wikipedia) gives 1970 for district formation

former_names: Tank tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan District
notes: Tank was a tehsil of Dera Ismail Khan District until 1992, when it became a district.
source_title: Tank District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Tank (PCO 2000)

former_names: Dir District (Dir State until 1969)
notes: Upper Dir is the remainder of Dir District after Lower Dir was separated in 1996, so existed_1972 and existed_1981 refer to the undivided Dir District under its former name; Dir State was merged in 1969 and became a district in 1970.
source_title: Upper Dir District (Wikipedia); Lower Dir District (Wikipedia) citing Deputy Commissioner Dir Lower; Dir (region) (Wikipedia)

former_names: Bajaur sub-division of Malakand Agency (from 1960); semi-independent area under the Political Agent Malakand before 1960
notes: Bajaur was declared a sub-division of Malakand Agency in 1960 and upgraded to a full agency on 1 December 1973 with its Political Agent at Khar; its parent is written as MALAKAND PROTECTED AREA because Malakand Agency has no other 1998-list name, and PCO nonetheless restated 1951-1972 populations onto the agency area.
source_title: Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74; GlobalSecurity 'Bajaur Agency' (https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/pakistan/fata-bajaur.htm); Dawn 2012 'Guarding the frontier'

notes: Khyber Agency was created by the British in 1879 and existed at every census; Mohmand Agency was separated from the charge of its Political Agent in 1951.
source_title: Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74

notes: Kurram was occupied by the British and declared an agency in 1892 and existed at every census.
source_title: Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74; Dawn, 'Guarding the frontier' (2012) (https://www.dawn.com/news/758168)

notes: Mohmand Agency was established in 1951 from the area previously under the administrative control of the Political Agent Khyber; the month was not found, so whether it existed at the February 1951 census is unclear although PCO restated a 1951 population onto it.
source_title: Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74; Dawn, 'Guarding the frontier' (2012) (https://www.dawn.com/news/758168); Mohmand District (Wikipedia)

former_names: Tochi Agency
notes: North Waziristan Agency was created on paper in 1895 and constituted as a full agency with headquarters at Miranshah in 1910; it was earlier called the Tochi Agency and existed at every census.
source_title: North Waziristan Agency (Wikipedia), citing Imperial Gazetteer of India 1908; Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74 (1910); List of districts in KP (Wikipedia) for the Tochi name

former_names: Frontier Region Kohat (part)
notes: Orakzai Agency was announced on 3 November 1973 and formally inaugurated on 1 December 1973 from territory previously administered as the Frontier Region of Kohat district by the Deputy Commissioner Kohat; PCO restated 1961 and 1972 populations onto it but has none for 1951.
source_title: GlobalSecurity 'Orakzai Agency'; Sarfraz Khan, 'Special Status of Tribal Areas (FATA): An Artificial Imperial Construct Bleeding Asia', Eurasia Border Review (Hokkaido Univ.), pp. 63-74; Orakzai District (Wikipedia); Dawn, 'Guarding the frontier' (2012)

former_names: Wana Agency
notes: South Waziristan Agency has functioned since 1895 (Khan dates a Waziristan Agency to 1885), was earlier called the Wana Agency, and existed at every census.
source_title: Dawn, 'Guarding the frontier' (2012); Dunya News 'Geography and brief history of South Waziristan' (https://dunyanews.tv/en/Pakistan/14440-Geography-and-brief-history-of-South-Waziristan); List of districts in KP (Wikipedia) for the Wana name

former_names: Frontier Region Bannu; Tribal Area Adjoining Bannu District
notes: Creation date not found; the Frontier Regions were tribal tracts administered by the Deputy Commissioner of the adjoining settled district and PCO gives no restated population for FR Bannu before 1998, so its separate existence at earlier censuses is unclear.
source_title: Frontier Regions (Wikipedia), citing FATA Secretariat 'Administrative System' (no creation dates)

former_names: Frontier Region Dera Ismail Khan; Tribal Area Adjoining D.I.Khan District
notes: Creation date not found; administered by the Deputy Commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan and PCO gives no restated population before 1998, so its separate existence at earlier censuses is unclear.
source_title: Frontier Regions (Wikipedia), citing FATA Secretariat 'Administrative System' (no creation dates)

former_names: Frontier Region Kohat; Tribal Area Adjoining Kohat District
notes: Creation date not found; it existed before 1973 because Orakzai Agency was carved out of it on 1 December 1973, but PCO gives no restated population before 1998 so its boundaries at earlier censuses are unclear.
source_title: GlobalSecurity 'Orakzai Agency' (Orakzai was part of FR Kohat until 30 Nov 1973); Frontier Regions (Wikipedia)

former_names: Frontier Region Lakki Marwat; Tribal Area Adjoining Lakki Marwat District
notes: Creation date not found; it is named after Lakki Marwat District, which was created on 1 July 1992, so it cannot have existed under this name at earlier censuses, and the parent FR BANNU is an inference from the Bhittani tract adjoining the former Bannu District that no source read here confirms.
source_title: Bettani Tehsil / FR Lakki Marwat (Wikipedia), citing FATA Secretariat 'Historical background and administrative profile of the FR Lakki Marwat' (not retrievable)

former_names: Frontier Region Peshawar; Tribal Area Adjoining Peshawar District
notes: Creation date not found; administered by the Deputy Commissioner of Peshawar and PCO gives no restated population before 1998, so its separate existence at earlier censuses is unclear.
source_title: Hassan Khel Tehsil / FR Peshawar (Wikipedia), citing FATA Secretariat profile and PCO '1998 census report of Tribal Area Adjoining Peshawar District' (2001)

former_names: Frontier Region Tank; Tribal Area Adjoining Tank District
notes: Creation date not found; it is named after Tank District (created 1992) but the Bhittani tract adjoining Tank was administered from Tank before that, and PCO gives no restated population before 1998, so its separate existence at earlier censuses is unclear.
source_title: Frontier Regions (Wikipedia), citing FATA Secretariat 'Administrative System' (no creation dates); Tank District (Wikipedia) for the 2018 merger of FR Tank

parent_districts_1998_names: ABBOTTABAD DISTRICT; HARIPUR DISTRICT; MANSEHRA DISTRICT; BATAGRAM DISTRICT; KOHISTAN DISTRICT (part)
former_names: Hazara District (British-era settled district; abolished 1976)
notes: Hazara was a British-era settled district (tehsils Abbottabad, Haripur, Mansehra, plus Batagram from 1955) that existed until 1976, when it was split into Abbottabad and Mansehra districts and Hazara became a division; its area corresponds to the 1998 districts Abbottabad, Haripur, Mansehra, Batagram and the Hazara part of Kohistan.
source_title: Hazara District (Wikipedia), citing 1998 District Census Report of Mansehra (PCO 2000) p. 1; Hazara Division (Wikipedia)

parent_districts_1998_names: UPPER DIR DISTRICT; LOWER DIR DISTRICT
former_names: Dir State (princely state under Malakand Agency)
notes: Dir State was merged in 1969 and declared a district in 1970; the undivided Dir District existed at the 1972 and 1981 censuses and was divided into Upper Dir and Lower Dir in 1996.
source_title: Dir (region) (Wikipedia); Lower Dir District (Wikipedia) citing Deputy Commissioner Dir Lower

parent_districts_1998_names: SWAT DISTRICT; BUNER DISTRICT; SHANGLA DISTRICT; UPPER DIR DISTRICT; LOWER DIR DISTRICT; CHITRAL DISTRICT; MALAKAND PROTECTED AREA; BAJAUR AGENCY
former_names: Malakand Agency (political agency covering Swat, Dir and Chitral states, the Malakand Protected Area and, from 1960, the Bajaur sub-division)
notes: Malakand Agency existed at the 1951 and 1961 censuses as the political agency over the princely states of Swat, Dir and Chitral, the Malakand Protected Area and (from 1960) the Bajaur sub-division; in 1970, after the 1969 merger of the states, it became Malakand Division, and PCO restated its 1951 and 1961 populations onto the successor units.
source_title: Malakand Agency (Wikipedia); Malakand Division (Wikipedia) citing Jamestown Foundation; GlobalSecurity 'Bajaur Agency' for the 1960 sub-division
